chunks: Hanzalah ibn Abī ʿĀmir al-Rāhib was martyred at Uḥud, and the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not command that he be given ghusl. He said, “I saw the angels between the heaven and the earth washing Hanzalah with water from the clouds in silver vessels,” and he used to be called Ghasīl al-Malāʾikah.

key_terms.غَسِيلَ ٱلْمَلَائِكَةِ: the one washed by the angels

ai.seo_question: Why was Ḥanẓalah ibn Abī ʿĀmir called Ghasīl al-Malāʾikah?
ai.summary: This report recounts the martyrdom of Ḥanẓalah ibn Abī ʿĀmir at Uḥud and states that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not order ghusl for him. It describes the angels washing him from heavenly water, which became the reason he was known as Ghasīl al-Malāʾikah.
